You will likely need to run `git fetch`. Starship only displays `$behind` if the local repository files already know that it is behind, it doesn't attempt to make any network requests. Many editors will regularly call `git fetch` in the background for you, and you can also configure your shell to handle this in the background.
For me, it didn't render `ahead` count or `diverged` either. I've noticed some missing. I did just switch to using a git worktree. Is that perhaps part of the problem?

Run to see if `git status` displays the status vs the remote repo. If it doesn’t, the problem lies in your Git configuration, not in Starship.

I had to run `git branch main -u origin/main` to fix this issue.
